subject: Private link: asymmetric return-path + fragmentation blackhole (Clearshore)

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Large file uploads failing over private link — intermittent timeouts

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing intermittent failures when our app tries to upload files > 4MB to the service over the private VPC link. The client POSTs often hang (TCP stalls) and then timeout after ~30s. It looks like retries sometimes succeed. This started after a maintenance window on our edge on Nov 30.

Symptoms:
- Successful small uploads (<512KB) 100% of the time, large uploads succeed ~30% of attempts.
- Server side logs show TCP retransmits, client side shows connection resets.
- We captured a pcap at the Clearshore edge during a failing transfer and attached packet_capture.pcap.

Can the Redwood side review? We're available for an emergency window today.

Thanks,
Clearshore Ops Team
---
Clearshore Systems 
ops@clearshore.com

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: ops@clearshore.com, sara.perez@edgeworks.net
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Large file uploads failing over private link — intermittent timeouts

Thanks for the heads-up and for the pcap. First-pass read: this looks like an asymmetric return-path combined with an MTU/fragmentation failure. A few asks so we can triage quickly:

1) Please run iperf3 (10s) in both directions across the private link and paste results.
2) From the Clearshore edge device please provide: `ip route show`, `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` (or vendor equivalent), and the exact peer-next-hop seen for the 198.51.100.0/24 block.
3) Can EdgeWorks (sara) attach the tcpdump file and include the first few frames showing ICMP error (if any). Look for ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) and the DF bit on the original packet.
4) On your app VM, run `ethtool -k <iface>` and `ifconfig` before/after the fail (to check offload flags and MTU).

Initial mitigation options we can apply from Redwood side if this confirms fragmentation/DF: clamp MSS on the NAT gateway, temporarily route return traffic via the same transit (prevent asymmetry), or enable temporary ICMP type 3 allow so PMTU can converge. Longer-term I'd like to check whether any middlebox is rewriting source IPs which is driving the asymmetric return path.

I'll take a look at the pcap now; looping in EdgeWorks and infra (vivek) for config context.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: Sara Perez <sara.perez@edgeworks.net>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, ops@clearshore.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Large file uploads failing over private link — intermittent timeouts

Jordan — attaching the full pcap (packet_capture.pcap) and a short excerpt below. We confirmed: when a large transfer stalls we see an ICMP "fragmentation needed" coming from 198.51.100.1 (Clearshore egress) back to the client, plus the original TCP has the DF bit set. That ICMP points to an MTU of ~1420 on one leg.

pcap excerpt (time, src -> dst, info):
08:14:22.123 10.11.5.2 > 198.51.100.42: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 29200, length 1460
08:14:22.140 198.51.100.1 > 10.11.5.2: ICMP 3/4 Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu 1420)
08:14:22.141 10.11.5.2 > 198.51.100.42: Flags [P.], seq 1:2921, ack 1, win 29200, length 1460

When we replay traffic toward Redwood-hosted endpoint we reproduce the fragmentation-needed message consistently. We also ran `ethtool -k` on the Clearshore app VM and it shows TSO/GSO enabled; setting those off reduced visible retransmits in a local test but wasn't a complete fix for large uploads.

Config snippets we see on the Clearshore edge: some address translation is happening — the NAT pool uses a port-preserving algorithm for certain prefixes; we suspect hairpinning + asymmetric next-hop after the Nov30 change. Attaching config-diff.txt (post-maintenance changes).

Let us know if you want EdgeWorks to flip any routes during a maintenance window.

— Sara Perez
Network Engineer, EdgeWorks
sara.perez@edgeworks.net

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: ops@clearshore.com, sara.perez@edgeworks.net
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Large file uploads failing over private link — intermittent timeouts

Thanks Sara — the pcap confirms two things we should treat as root contributors: 1) ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag-needed) is returned with DF set; 2) reply traffic for the 10.11.5.0/24 (Clearshore internal) is occasionally egressing via a different next-hop due to source IP rewrite at the edge, which creates an asymmetric return path and prevents early PMTU discovery.

Concrete steps / mitigations I recommend now (ordered by risk/speed):
A) Immediate, low-risk (no config rollback on Clearshore): on Redwood NAT gateway for the Clearshore customer route, enable MSS clamping to 1400. This prevents the host from sending large DF-marked segments.
B) Clearshore: temporarily open ICMP type 3/code 4 from your edge to allow PMTU to converge while we investigate the NAT rewrite.
C) EdgeWorks: if possible, revert the post-maintenance route that reorders egress for the Clearshore prefix to the previous path for a 1-hour window; if return traffic is forced back to the same transit the fragmentation errors stop reproducing.
D) On the Clearshore app VM(s): disable TSO/GSO/TCP segmentation offload for test window and re-run upload tests to validate (this is low impact but requires process restart on some VMs).
E) Medium-term: change NAT algorithm to preserve original source prefix mapping (avoid address rewrite that changes return-path). Consider expanding ephemeral port range if we hit port collisions on certain NAT pools.

I can apply (A) from our side within 15 minutes if Clearshore approves. Please confirm a short window and I'll schedule. After we stabilize I propose a joint postmortem with the packet captures and config diffs.

Jordan Blake
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
